title: Add model fingerprinter and annotated timeline exporter for release-note seeds
author: Asha Menon
release_notes:
- Introduces a deterministic model 'fingerprinter' used to create compact, stable IDs for model variant metadata.
- Adds an 'annotated timeline exporter' CLI that generates human-readable timeline seeds for release-note automation.
- Backwards-compatible: fingerprint schema is additive and stored alongside existing metadata.
- Includes unit tests and docs for onboarding teams to use fingerprints in changelog generation.
body:
Motivation:
We need a lightweight, deterministic way to identify when a model's serving characteristics (architecture, tokenizer, quantization flags, compile options) have changed in ways that warrant a changelog entry or a regression gate. Current onboarding relies on free-text notes and ad-hoc diffs which makes automated release-note drafting brittle.

What this PR does (single continuous description):
This change introduces two pieces: 1) a model fingerprinter that computes a compact stable fingerprint from canonicalized model metadata + a small structural digest (tokenizer spec, top-level config keys, layer shape summary and quantization buckets). The fingerprinter is implemented as a pure function with a JSON schema-backed output (fingerprint:v1) so it can be stored in the registry and used by downstream tooling. 2) an annotated timeline exporter CLI that walks a model's onboard history (versions, artifacts, profile snapshots) and produces a compact, annotated timeline intended as a seed for release-note automation. The exporter groups changes by semantic buckets (performance, API/IO surface, compliance/keys, packaging) using simple heuristics and includes the computed fingerprint delta per version to highlight mechanical changes vs. editorial notes.

Technical details and design decisions:
- Fingerprinter: deterministic canonicalization (stable key ordering, normalizing floats to 4 decimal places where applicable), then BLAKE3-256 hashing of the canonical blob. The resulting fingerprint contains the hash and a short trait vector (e.g., tokenization=bytepair-v2, quant=8bit, layers=20-12-12). The trait vector is intentionally human-readable to aid triage.
- Schema: added schema/models/fingerprint_v1.json and a small adapter to persist the fingerprint in registry metadata as metadata.fingerprint.v1. This is additive.
- Exporter: CLI at tools/timeline_exporter/export_timeline.py that accepts model name/version range and outputs a newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) timeline with annotations and suggested release-note bullets. The exporter uses a small heuristic engine (rules/rule-set.yaml) that assigns change categories and confidence scores. Rule set is conservative by default to avoid noisy notes.
- Tests: unit tests for canonicalization, hash stability across unrelated metadata reordering, and integration test that runs the exporter against a small fixture history.
- Docs: docs/registry/fingerprints.md and docs/registry/timeline_exporter.md with examples and suggested CI hooks.

Changed files (high level):
- src/registry/fingerprinter.py (new)
- schema/models/fingerprint_v1.json (new)
- tools/timeline_exporter/export_timeline.py (new)
- tools/timeline_exporter/rules/rule-set.yaml (new)
- tests/registry/test_fingerprinter.py (new)

- docs/registry/fingerprints.md (new)
- docs/registry/timeline_exporter.md (new)
- registry/db/migrations/202502_add_fingerprint_column.sql (new)
- examples/onboard/fixture_small_history.ndjson (new)
- Makefile: add 'timeline-export' target (mod)

Commit summary:
- a1f3c7d: add fingerprinter implementation + canonicalizer
- b2d4f90: fingerprint schema + persistence adapter
- d3e77b1: exporter CLI and rule-set draft
- e9f14b5: tests for fingerprinter and exporter integration
- fa02b88: docs and Makefile target

Review conversation (high level and kept concise as a continuous string):
Diego Alvarez: "Nice approach — canonicalization + blake3 makes sense. One concern: trait vector might leak internal hyperparams we don't want surfaced. Can we whitelist fields?"
Asha Menon (author): "Agree. I added a whitelist with explicit allowed keys and a transform map for common renames (see whitelist in fingerprinter.py). Trait vector only contains low-risk, high-signal keys (tokenizer family, quantization bucket, layer_counts)."
Priya Nandagopal: "Integration test looks good, but the migration needs a safe rollback. Can you add a migration down script and a short note about backfilling for existing entries?"
Asha Menon: "Added 202502_add_fingerprint_column_down.sql and a short note in the migration file; backfill script is optional and documented in the fingerprints.md with a recommended backfill recovered via a batch job (we didn't include a heavy backfill here)."
Liam O'Connor: "CI flagged a lint failure on export_timeline argument parsing."
Asha Menon: "Fixed in b7d2c3a, re-ran tests. All CI checks green."
Diego Alvarez: "Approved after confirming whitelist and tests."

CI summary: initial run had lint error and one flaky test; fixes applied in follow-up commit, full CI green on final run.

Migration/backwards compatibility note:
The fingerprint is stored under metadata.fingerprint.v1. The code will tolerate missing fingerprints (older models). The schema is additive and the registry UI will show a generated fingerprint column only when present; there is a documented recommended backfill procedure for large registries but it is intentionally opt-in to avoid long blocking migrations.

How this helps product teams:
- Release engineers can now automatically detect mechanical deltas that matter for changelogs (e.g., quantization changed from 16->8, tokenizer swapped) and generate safe draft bullets.
- Platform teams can gate rollouts with simple fingerprint-equality checks to avoid serving surprises.

Follow-ups / TODOs (short list):
- Add an RFC to standardize the trait whitelist across registries and onboarding tools (ENG-4205).
- Add a light-weight backfill job template for very large registries (optional).
- Consider adding a confidence-calibrated classifier to the exporter to reduce manual triage over time.

Notes about uniqueness compared to previous registry work: this intentionally focuses on a compact, human-readable trait vector combined with a stable digest and a separate timeline export format designed for automated note seeding, rather than a large changelog assembler or release provenance ledger. The goal is to make small, reliable automation steps available to release writers and platform teams without introducing heavy provenance bundles.
